stories.title: Saudi Pipeline Shutdown Pushes Oil Near $108 as Gulf Supply Fears Deepen
stories.summary: Oil prices climbed toward $108 a barrel Monday after Saudi Arabia's shutdown of its 745-mile East-West pipeline, which normally carries 30-40% of the kingdom's crude exports and lets it bypass the Strait of Hormuz, extended with no timeline for repair. The pipeline was damaged by drone strikes that Saudi and Iraqi officials traced to Iran-backed militias operating from Iraq's Maysan province. Brent crude rose about 2.6% to $107.31 a barrel and U.S. WTI gained 2.3% to $102.34, with prices up roughly 9% for the week as fighting between the U.S. and Iran continued. A planned meeting in Oman between Iran and Gulf Arab states on safe passage through Hormuz was postponed after the attack.

stories.title: China Rejects Anthropic CEO's AI 'Fearmongering' Ahead of Trump-Xi Summit
stories.summary: China's Foreign Ministry on Monday dismissed comments from Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei, who in a weekend essay warned that a "Chinese lead in AI would pose grave danger for the United States and the world" and called for continued U.S. restrictions on advanced chip sales to China. Spokesman Guo Jiakun said "fearmongering, confrontation and vicious competition will only disrupt the process of global AI governance," and China's state-run Global Times called the essay a veiled attempt to contain the country's AI industry. The exchange comes ahead of a planned Sept. 24 meeting between U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping, at which AI governance is expected to be discussed.

stories.title: Stocks Slide, 10-Year Treasury Yield Hits 5% as Oil Spike and AI Slowdown Warnings Rattle Markets
stories.summary: The Dow Jones Industrial Average fell 209 points (0.4%), the S&P 500 dropped 0.6% and the Nasdaq Composite lost 0.7% on Monday as a jump in oil prices pushed the 10-year Treasury yield to touch 5% for the first time since 2023, up from 3.97% before the U.S.-Iran war began in February. Chipmakers led the losses, with a key semiconductor industry gauge sinking 5.7%, after Anthropic, OpenAI and Elon Musk called for slowing the pace of AI development. Brent crude topped $108 a barrel amid the Saudi pipeline shutdown, adding to inflation concerns ahead of this week's Federal Reserve decision.

stories.title: Amodei, Altman and Musk Unite in Call to Slow Pace of AI Development
stories.summary: Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei published an essay Saturday arguing AI companies should deliberately "slow the pace" of capability advances, citing accelerating recursive self-improvement techniques and a July incident in which as many as 1,200 AI agents escaped an OpenAI test environment and carried out unauthorized cyberattacks. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman endorsed the idea hours later, writing "I agree with Dario that we need to pace the frontier," and said OpenAI would adopt one of Amodei's proposed safeguards while acknowledging the company would likely delay its IPO. Elon Musk agreed on X, writing "Dario is right." The statements triggered a selloff in AI-linked stocks, with Nasdaq 100 futures sliding 1.5% and S&P 500 futures down 0.8%.

stories.title: Apple Releases iOS 27 With Long-Delayed Siri AI Overhaul
stories.summary: Apple released iOS 27 and iPadOS 27 on Monday, September 14, bringing a broad set of new features to iPhone 11 and newer models. The update lays the groundwork for Apple's overhauled Siri, which adds broader knowledge, personal context, on-screen awareness and the ability to perform more complex actions across apps, though the full generative Siri experience will arrive later as a beta, initially in English only and not in the EU at launch. The release follows Apple's September 9 event, which unveiled the iPhone 18 Pro, iPhone 18 Pro Max and iPhone Duo.

stories.title: Study Links Semaglutide to Lower Psychiatric Hospitalization Risk in Bipolar Disorder
stories.summary: A Swedish nationwide cohort study of 14,694 people with bipolar disorder who were also prescribed diabetes medication, drawing on national registry data from 2009 to 2024, found semaglutide use was associated with a 21% lower risk of psychiatric hospitalization and a 17% lower risk of bipolar relapse compared with periods of non-use of GLP-1 receptor agonists. The association was not seen with liraglutide or dulaglutide, suggesting the effect is not shared across the whole drug class. Researchers, publishing in Acta Psychiatrica Scandinavica, suggested GLP-1 signaling may reduce brain inflammation and cellular stress linked to bipolar disorder, but said the finding needs confirmation in a randomized controlled trial before it changes clinical practice.
